extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy, moral and social theory (general educated audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of criteria and causal explanations for honour, dishonour, worthiness, manners, and the origins/nature of religion as presented in a political-philosophical chapter (Hobbesian). It lists what actions/qualities count as honourable or dishonourable and gives natural motivations for human manners and religion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience as Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: To obey, is to Honour; because no man obeys them, whom they think have no power to help, or hurt them. And consequently to disobey, is to Dishonour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obedience functions as a public sign of the other's power; disobedience signals lack of respect and thus dishonour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts as Honour or Dishonour
rubrics_metrics.description: To give great gifts to a man, is to Honour him; ... To give little gifts, is to Dishonour; because it is but Almes, and signifies an opinion of the need of small helps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large gifts acknowledge power/protection; small gifts imply condescension or charity and therefore lessen honour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting another's good / Flattery as Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: To be sedulous in promoting another's good; also to flatter, is to Honour; as a signe we seek his protection or ayde.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively advancing someone's interests (even by flattery) is treated as a submission acknowledging their power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect as Dishonour
rubrics_metrics.description: To neglect, is to Dishonour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to attend to someone or their interests signals devaluation and thus dishonour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giving way/place as Honour; Arrogation as Dishonour
rubrics_metrics.description: To give way, or place to another, in any Commodity, is to Honour; ... To arrogate, is to Dishonour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yielding precedence or position publicly confers honour; taking it presumptuously is dishonourable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing love or fear as Honour; Contempt as Dishonour
rubrics_metrics.description: To shew any signe of love, or feare of another, is to Honour; ... To contemne, or lesse to love or feare then he expects, is to Dishonour; for ’tis undervaluing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affective signs (love, fear) indicate valuation of another's power; failing to exhibit expected affect counts as slights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Praise as Honour; Revile/Mock/Pity as Dishonour
rubrics_metrics.description: To praise, magnifie, or call happy, is to Honour; ... To revile, mock, or pitty, is to Dishonour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approbation raises perceived status; derision or pity lowers it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerate speech, decency, humility as Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: To speak to another with consideration, to appear before him with decency, and humility, is to Honour him; ... To speak to him rashly, to do anything before him obscenely, slovenly, impudently, is to Dishonour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manner and comportment are signals of respect; rude or improper behavior publicly dishonours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust and Reliance as Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: To believe, to trust, to rely on another, is to Honour him; signe of opinion of his vertue and power. To distrust, or not believe, is to Dishonour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epistemic and practical reliance manifest esteem for someone's capacities and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attending to Counsel as Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: To hearken to a mans counsell, or discourse of what kind soever, is to Honour; as a signe we think him wise, or eloquent, or witty. To sleep, or go forth, or talk the while, is to Dishonour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active listening signals deference; inattention signals contempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming to Local Signs of Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: To do those things to another, which he takes for signes of Honour, or which the Law or Custome makes so, is to Honour; ... To refuse to do them, is to Dishonour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honour is partly conventional: complying with a person's or society's recognized signs of respect affirms their standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement in Opinion as Honour; Dissent as Dishonour
rubrics_metrics.description: To agree with in opinion, is to Honour; ... To dissent, is Dishonour; and an upbraiding of errour; and (if the dissent be in many things) of folly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public concurrence functions as endorsement of someone's judgement; repeated dissent implies that person is mistaken or foolish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation as Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: To imitate, is to Honour; for it is vehemently to approve. To imitate ones Enemy, is to Dishonour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copying someone's habits or style is the highest form of flattery and recognition; copying foes is contemptuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honouring Those Another Honours (and Not Their Enemies)
rubrics_metrics.description: To honour those another honours, is to Honour him; as a signe of approbation of his judgement. To honour his Enemies, is to Dishonour him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associative respect: aligning your honours with someone else's affirms their discernment; honouring their enemies contradicts it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment in Counsel or Difficult Actions as Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: To employ in counsell, or in actions of difficulty, is to Honour; ... To deny employment in the same cases, to those that seek it, is to Dishonour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment to responsible tasks publicly recognizes ability and power; refusal to appoint is a slight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign-Defined Civil Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: A Soveraigne doth Honour a Subject, with whatsoever Title, or Office, or Employment, or Action, that he himselfe will have taken for a signe of his will to Honour him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil honours are determined by the supreme authority; formal titles/offices function as state-sanctioned signs of honour (example: Persian king's conduct of Mordecai).

rubrics_metrics.name: Honour as Sign of Power
rubrics_metrics.description: Honourable is whatsoever possession, action, or quality, is an argument and signe of Power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The central principle: honour indexes perceived power (capacity to help or hurt); anything that signals power tends to be honourable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular Metrics of Honour (fortune, riches, qualities, vice)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be Honoured, loved, or feared of many, is Honourable; ... Good fortune (if lasting,) Honourable; ... Riches, are Honourable; ... Magnanimity, Liberality, Hope, Courage, Confidence, are Honourable; Pusillanimity, Parsimony, Fear, Diffidence, are Dishonourable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists common attributes and states that increase or decrease perceived honour—social recognition, wealth, courage, and magnanimity raise honour; poverty and timidity lower it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely Resolution vs Irresolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely Resolution, or determination of what a man is to do, is Honourable; ... And Irresolution, Dishonourable; as a signe of too much valuing of little impediments...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisiveness indicates contempt of minor risks and is honoured; hesitancy indicates pusillanimity and is dishonourable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience, Science, Discretion, Wit vs Error and Folly
rubrics_metrics.description: All Actions, and Speeches, that proceed, or seem to proceed from much Experience, Science, Discretion, or Wit, are Honourable; ... Actions, or Words that proceed from Errour, Ignorance, or Folly, Dishonourable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence and prudence are honored whether in speech or deed; mistakes and ignorance provoke dishonour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine Gravity vs Feigned Gravity
rubrics_metrics.description: Gravity, as farre forth as it seems to proceed from a mind employed on some thing else, is Honourable; because employment is a signe of Power. But if it seem to proceed from a purpose to appear grave, it is Dishonourable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic seriousness (engagement) confers honour; pretended seriousness is contemptible (ship metaphors: laden ship vs ballasted with sand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuousness and Descent as Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: To be Conspicuous, that is to say, to be known, for Wealth, Office, great Actions, or any eminent Good, is Honourable; On the contrary, Obscurity, is Dishonourable. To be descended from conspicuous Parents, is Honourable; ... obscure Parentage, is Dishonourable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visibility and prestigious lineage elevate honour because they signal accumulated power or advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity with Loss vs Craft and Shifting
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions proceeding from Equity, joyned with losse, are Honourable; ... On the contrary, Craft, Shifting, neglect of Equity, is Dishonourable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-sacrificial fairness is a sign of magnanimity (and thus honour); clever but dishonest gain corrodes honour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honour Independent of Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor does it alter the case of Honour, whether an action (so it be great and difficult, and consequently a signe of much power,) be just or unjust: for Honour consisteth onely in the opinion of Power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbesian claim: honour tracks perceived power, not moral rightness—great but unjust acts can be celebrated if they display power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Commonwealth Honour: Piracy and Duels
rubrics_metrics.description: Also amongst men, till there were constituted great Common-wealths, it was thought no dishonour to be a Pyrate, or a High-way Theefe; ... private Duels are, and alwayes will be Honourable, though unlawfull, till such time as there shall be Honour ordained for them that refuse, and Ignominy for them that make the Challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context matters: what counts as honour depends on social institutions; practices criminalized by law can nonetheless be honoured in other normative orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hereditary Arms and Gentry
rubrics_metrics.description: Scutchions, and coats of Armes haereditary, where they have any eminent Priviledges, are Honourable; otherwise not: ... This kind of Honour, commonly called Gentry, has been derived from the Antient Germans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heraldic marks confer honour only insofar as they signal real privileges or power; their social meaning is historically contingent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of Honour as Signs of Sovereign Value
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of Honour, such as are Duke, Count, Marquis, and Baron, are Honourable; as signifying the value set upon them by the Soveraigne Power of the Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles originate as offices of military or administrative command and become honorifics when institutionalized; they mark precedence and sovereign favor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worthiness / Fitnesse (Definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: WORTHINESSE, is a thing different from the worth, or value of a man; and also from his merit, or desert; and consisteth in a particular power, or ability, for that, whereof he is said to be worthy: which particular ability, is usually named FITNESSE, or Aptitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worthiness is functional fitness for an office or role; merit presupposes a right to the thing deserved, whereas worthiness is about aptitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners Defined (broad social qualities)
rubrics_metrics.description: By MANNERS, I mean not here, Decency of behaviour; ... But those qualities of man-kind, that concern their living together in Peace, and Unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manners here refers to the dispositions and institutions that enable social coexistence (not merely small personal etiquette).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restless Desire of Power
rubrics_metrics.description: A perpetuall and restlesse desire of Power after power, that ceaseth onely in Death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human nature inclines toward accumulation and securing of power; this explains much of political behavior (kings codify power into laws, then seek other ends).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition Produces Contention and Reverence of Antiquity
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition of Riches, Honour, command, or other power, enclineth to Contention, Enmity, and War: ... particularly, competition of praise, enclineth to a reverence of Antiquity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rivalry over status and resources leads to conflict; esteem for ancestors is a strategy to undercut rivals by invoking tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Obedience from Desire of Ease and Fear
rubrics_metrics.description: Desire of Ease, and sensuall Delight, disposeth men to obey a common Power: ... Fear of Death, and Wounds, disposeth to the same...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prudential motives—seeking comfort and avoiding harm—drive people to accept centralized authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desire of Knowledge/Arts and Praise as Motives for Obedience and Virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Desire of Knowledge, and Arts of Peace, enclineth men to obey a common Power: ... Desire of Praise, disposeth to laudable actions, such as please them whose judgement they value; ... Desire of Fame after death does the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intellectual and reputational incentives encourage cooperation and morally praised behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hatred from Inability to Requite Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: To have received from one, to whom we think our selves equall, greater benefits than there is hope to Requite, disposeth to counterfiet love; but really secret hatred...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unreciprocated obligations toward equals can generate resentment rather than gratitude; relationship of relative status affects the emotional response to gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fear and Distrust as Prompts to Preemptive Harm and Coalition
rubrics_metrics.description: Feare of oppression, disposeth a man to anticipate, or to seek ayd by society: ... Men that distrust their own subtilty, are in tumult, and sedition, better disposed for victory, than they that suppose themselves wise, or crafty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perceived threats push actors toward collective defense or preemption; strategic psychology matters for political mobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vain-glory and Ambition: Different Behavioral Tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Vain-glorious men ... are enclined onely to ostentation; but not to attempt... Vain-glorious men ... are enclined to rash engaging; ... Men that have a strong opinion of their own wisdome ... are disposed to Ambition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-deceptive pride tends either to mere show or to reckless action; genuine confidence in competence motivates pursuit of public office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pusillanimity and Frugality as Limits on Collective Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Pusillanimity disposeth men to Irresolution ... Frugality,(though in poor men a Vertue,) maketh a man unapt to atchieve such actions, as require the strength of many men at once: For it weakeneth their Endeavour...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain personal dispositions (excessive caution, stinginess) undermine the willingness to undertake risky collective enterprises that require mobilization and reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence in Others from Eloquence/Flattery and Ignorance of Causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Eloquence, with flattery, disposeth men to confide in them that have it ... Want of Science, that is, Ignorance of causes, disposeth, or rather constraineth a man to rely on the advise, and authority of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persuasive presentation and epistemic dependence create followership even absent genuine competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Custom from Ignorance of Right and Causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ignorance of the causes, and originall constitution of Right, Equity, Law, and Justice, disposeth a man to make Custome and Example the rule of his actions ... receding from custome when their interest requires it...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Custom and precedent become default guides for action when deeper understanding of justice or causes is lacking; but this adherence is instrumental and mutable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credulity and Lying from Ignorance of Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Ignorance of naturall causes disposeth a man to Credulity, so as to believe many times impossibilities: ... And Credulity, because men love to be hearkened unto in company, disposeth them to lying...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of causal understanding fuels superstitious belief and falsehoods, which spread for social reasons (attention, status).

rubrics_metrics.name: Curiosity for Future Advantage and its Link to Religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Anxiety for the future time, disposeth men to enquire into the causes of things: because the knowledge of them, maketh men the better able to order the present to their best advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical concern about uncertain futures motivates both scientific inquiry and religious speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural Seeds of Religion (fourfold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinion of Ghosts, Ignorance of second causes, Devotion towards what men fear, and Taking of things Casuall for Prognostiques, consisteth the Naturall seed of Religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes identifies four psychological/cognitive roots that generate religion; each seed is then cultivated into diverse religious systems by cultural agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious Acts Mirror Human Honour Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: For the worship which naturally men exhibite to Powers invisible, it can be no other, but such expressions of their reverence, as they would use towards men; Gifts, Petitions, Thanks, Submission of Body, Considerate Addresses, sober Behaviour, premeditated Words, Swearing ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious rites replicate social gestures of deference—religion borrows the grammar of honour to structure worship and obedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two Modes of Cultivating Religion: Human and Divine Politiques
rubrics_metrics.description: These seeds have received culture from two sorts of men. One sort ... nourished, and ordered them, according to their own invention. The other, have done it, by Gods commandement, and direction: ... So that the Religion of the former sort, is a part of humane Politiques; and teacheth part of the duty which Earthly Kings require of their Subjects. And the Religion of the later sort is Divine Politiques;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes religion engineered for political ends from religion claimed as divine authority; both shape obedience and social order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurdity and Variability of Gentile Deifications
rubrics_metrics.description: There is almost nothing that has a name, that has not been esteemed amongst the Gentiles, in one place or another, a God, or Divell; ... The Heaven, the Ocean, the Planets, the Fire, the Earth, the Winds, were so many Gods. Men, Women, a Bird, a Crocodile, a Calf, a Dogge, a Snake, an Onion, a Leeke, a Deified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes catalogs the wide variety of objects worshipped across cultures to argue that religious objects and rites are culturally constructed and often arbitrary.
